posts.cooked:
So I was going through older topics and I found this one http://greaterthangames.com/forum/topic/dead-heroes-and-incapacitated-sides-2734 about hero deaths.

This interesting line to me was this one "So from what I remember, it was mentioned by Christopher in a podcast interview that 3 heroes die in the main Sentinels timeline."

So forum veterens is this really something Chistopher said? Is it still true or has it been retconed?

 

I'm going to make three assumptions: 1) That this is legit. 2) That the Sentinels Timeline is referring to just the Card game. 3) That we are just considering the main timeline not the Iron Legacy timeline (where additional hereos have died, Bunker and Unity at least).

At the time it seems that Legacy was considered one of the 3 and while he does die in an alternate timeline the Legacy of the main timeline not only survives but is around for Tactics as well.

So who are the three? Here are some choices.

1) Mr Fixer, we have confirmation with the Dark Watch Promos that he did die. As is common in comic books... he got better. "The hero team known as Dark Watch has gone through a lot. They were originally formed by Expatriette, Setback, and NightMist who were seeking to uncover the truth behind the events of the death of their friend, Mister Fixer." http://greaterthangames.com/content/sentinel-tactics-dark-watch

2) Legacy, he is still a possibility as I believe there was a comic arc where he did die (like the incapacitated side of his card) but the Iron Legacy arc changed that and he ends up surviving. Very comic bookish. "In this timeline... (Other stuff)...Years later, Felicia Parsons was the best prepared to accept her father's death at the hands of Baron Blade." http://www.kickstarter.com/projects/gtgames/sentinels-of-the-multiverse-shattered-timelines/posts/357311

3) Ra, the human using the powers of Ra seems to be different than Blake Washington in Tactics, did Washinton die and that is why someone else has taken up the staff?

4) Scholor, this has no basis behind it but it seems from his promo that things are getting worse for him. "John Rhodes has learned far too much and seen too deeply. He now acts as a gate between reality and the infinite void. He cannot protect himself, but can he protect his allies from what is yet to come?" http://greaterthangames.com/content/promos-and-oversized-cards-and-more

5) Someone else?

 

Let me know what you think, or debunk this podcast rumor.

posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked:
The problem is that the Sentinels Multiverse, like so many comic book universes, has many states that could be considered death, but maybe not.

 

Legacy dies, but not in the main timeline.  Does that count?

Something happens to Nightmist, and she turns into a cloud of mist (or leaves one behind, or something).  Does that count?

Ra is replaced by another Ra.  We have no idea what the mechanism behind that change was, whether that required the death of Blake Washington or not.

Unity was replaced by Golem Unity, which may or may not actually be her.  But in the future, and possibly not in this timeline.

 

That said, I think that the three best candidtates for "three character deaths" would be Mr. Fixer, Nightmist, and Ra.  But it's hard to say for certain.

I think the statement was 3 characters from the base set will die. I think we can pretty much assume Blake Washington is one of them, considering there is a new Ra in Tactics. I also think Legacy is counted, as he was supposed to die in this timeline, but thanks to Iron Legacy arriving, it prevented that death. Also continueing with Tactics as a reference, neither Grand Warlord Voss or Haka have made an appearance. It has since been confirmed that Voss will appear, but we would not recognize him. Considering Legacy most likely counts towards the death count, it is possible that Voss also dies where he is banished to and gains a new body or even he gets his old body back that has been transformed in some way. Also, Haka was confirmed to be able to live long enough to be at the FInal Wasteland. Does this mean he does not die? We'll just have to keep waiting to see.

It's also entirely possible that this has changed, as far as I can recall, he has only ever said it once. Which occured on a podcast somewhere within the first year of SotM's release. Probably even prior to the release of Tactics. Perhaps Legacy wasn't originally going to be as injured in the Iron Legacy fight, allowing him to go to the Wagner Mars Base, where he would die instead of Young Legacy. But with them getting approached about Sentinel Tactics, but they wanted Legacy in it more than they wanted to stick with Legacy's death, so the altered the story to fit it. Same with Voss, perhaps he was intended to die when he was sent, but his fan base kept him from dieing. Though he instead becomes horribly disfigured in exchange for his life.

The Staff of Ra gives three things to it's holder: the power, knowledge, and the personality of the god of the sun.

If the new guy posesses the Staff of Ra, shouldn't he have gained the knowledge and personality of Ra as well as his power? Yeah he knows how to use it's power, but I don't think he has the boundless knowledge of the Egyptian hero. And he certainly doesn't talk like Ra either. Where are these other 'gifts' of the staff?

I think he doesn't have these gifts because Blake Washington still posesses the spirit of Ra, meaning he's still alive out there somewhere.

posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
Thoughts On Ra:

I did a Footenotes piece on Beard Ra and what the historical context was behind the name. Long story short is that there is a death/resurection theme and a specific journy Ra takes into the underworld to die only to return reborn. Ra's initial defeat at the hands of the Ennead was a figurative death for him which sent him away for many years wandering the desert. Beard Ra was the resurection. A mucher stronger version of the Ra we previously knew. But what should interest everyone is the middle part that's missing, the details of the journey that led from the metaphoric death and resurection.

My current hypothesis on this journey is that like in the history books, our Ra also travels to the underworld (which we know exists in the Sentiels Universe thanks to the Tomb of Anubis environment deck. Anubis is seen with Ammit and the scales which weigh a pure heart). To become reborn into something more powerful than he was to save his friends Blake Washington likely had to give something up. A trade, if you will. Resurection is never without cost, a theme Christopher has played around with multiple times with Nightmist, Fixer, Operative, Pike, Spite, ect. The question becomes, "what did Blake have to give up?"

 

Thoughts on Dead Heros:

1. Blake Washington (Ra): I think this is the "gimmi" of the group.

2. Nightmist: The miststorm in Tactics and the Dark Watch bios do not make it sound like Nightmist made it out unscathed.

3. Scholar: The short sentence bio for the new Scholar of the Infinite promo is fairly damning of Johns fate. 

 

Now, Ronway might be correct that the quote wasn't that "3 heros will die from the card game" but that it's "3 characters from the base set will die". I do not remember the podcast well enough. But if he is, the list is as follows:

1. Blake Washington (Ra): Again, this is a "gimmi"

2. Voss: We know he was banished from this realm by Nightmist. Does that count as a death? Not sure, but it's the closest thing we have that we know about from the base set.

3. Haka: The only character from the base set to never be mentioned or seen in any current Tactics art/flavor text. If Ronway is right about the nature of the quote, then this will have to be true as a confirmed death (but again, I'm not sold that it is)

I don't think Golem Unity is Unity, and I don't think she was made by Unity.
